title: The Lie Group Exponential ℝ → S¹
content: Defines `circleMap : ℝ → ℂ` as `t ↦ exp(it)`. This single line is the entire Lie group exponential map for the circle group: a smooth (in fact, real-analytic) map from the additive Lie algebra ℝ ≅ iℝ ⊆ ℂ to the multiplicative Lie group S¹ ⊆ ℂˣ. Marked `noncomputable` because `Complex.exp` is defined as a power series limit.
mathContext: $\text{circleMap}(t) := e^{it} = \exp(it) \in \mathbb{C}$. The factor of $i$ embeds the real line as the imaginary axis, the canonical Lie algebra of $S^1$.

title: Homomorphism Property from exp_add
content: The homomorphism law `circleMap (a+b) = circleMap a · circleMap b` follows in three lines from the exponential addition law `Complex.exp_add`. After distributing `(↑(a+b))·I = ↑a·I + ↑b·I`, the equation reduces to `exp(z+w) = exp z · exp w`. This is the algebraic content of the entire Lie-group statement; everything else (continuity, kernel, surjectivity) is structure layered on top.
mathContext: $e^{i(a+b)} = e^{ia + ib} = e^{ia} \cdot e^{ib}$. The exponential addition law $e^{z+w} = e^z e^w$ for complex $z, w$ is itself a consequence of the absolute convergence of the exp power series and the binomial theorem.

title: Inverse Element via exp_neg
content: `circleMap (-t) = (circleMap t)⁻¹` follows from `Complex.exp_neg : exp(-z) = (exp z)⁻¹` after rewriting `((-t : ℝ) : ℂ) · I = -((t : ℝ) · I)` using `push_cast; ring`. This pair of identities (homomorphism + inverse) is exactly what's needed to package `circleMap` as a `MonoidHom`. Note the cast bookkeeping: `push_cast` is needed to move negation through the `ℝ → ℂ` coercion.
mathContext: $e^{-it} = (e^{it})^{-1}$. Combined with $e^{i(a+b)} = e^{ia}e^{ib}$, this gives the full group law on $S^1$.

title: Bridge to Euler's Formula
content: The connection back to the parent file: `circleMap t = cos t + i·sin t` is exactly Euler's formula, imported from `EulerIdentityOQ01OQ01.euler_formula`. This file rests on that axiom-free Taylor-series proof. Without it, `circleMap` would be opaque; with it, the trigonometric form unlocks the kernel and surjectivity proofs in §5–§6.
mathContext: $e^{it} = \cos t + i \sin t$ — Euler's formula, the foundational identity linking analysis (exponential power series) and trigonometry (cosine and sine power series).

title: Image Lies on the Unit Circle
content: The image of `circleMap` lies in $S^1 = \{z : \|z\| = 1\}$, proved in two lines using `Complex.norm_exp_ofReal_mul_I`. The corollary `circleMap_ne_zero` (used to construct the `Units.mk0` in §3) follows: if `circleMap t = 0` then `‖circleMap t‖ = 0`, contradicting `‖circleMap t‖ = 1`. This is what lets us build a `MonoidHom` into `ℂˣ` rather than just `ℂ`.
mathContext: $|e^{it}| = 1$ for all real $t$. Equivalently, $e^{it} \cdot \overline{e^{it}} = e^{it} \cdot e^{-it} = 1$, exhibiting $e^{it}$ as an element of $U(1) = S^1$.

title: Packaging as a Mathlib MonoidHom
content: `circleHom : Multiplicative ℝ →* ℂˣ` is the formal Lie-group statement. The Mathlib idiom for an additive→multiplicative homomorphism is `Multiplicative ℝ →* G`, where `Multiplicative ℝ` is a type-level wrapper carrying the multiplicative structure on the additive group ℝ. The construction uses `Units.mk0` (since `circleMap t ≠ 0`), and `map_one'`/`map_mul'` reduce to `circleMap_zero` and `circleMap_add` after unfolding `Multiplicative.toAdd`. The chained `show` tactics navigate the type isomorphism.
mathContext: Formally: $\text{circleHom} \in \text{Hom}_{\mathbf{Grp}}((\mathbb{R}, +), (\mathbb{C}^\times, \cdot))$. The wrapping into `ℂˣ` (units) rather than just `ℂ` is essential because `MonoidHom` targets must be groups under multiplication, and `ℂ` is only a monoid (zero has no inverse).

title: Continuity → Topological Group Homomorphism
content: Continuity of `circleMap` is the composition of `Complex.continuous_exp` with continuity of `t ↦ ↑t · I` (which is `continuous_ofReal.mul continuous_const`). Combined with the homomorphism property, this exhibits `circleHom` as a continuous group homomorphism — equivalently, a topological group homomorphism, equivalently the Lie group exponential. In Lie theory, smoothness comes for free here because `exp` is real-analytic.
mathContext: $t \mapsto e^{it}$ is continuous (in fact, $C^\infty$ and real-analytic) as a map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$. The composition $\mathbb{R} \xrightarrow{t \mapsto it} \mathbb{C} \xrightarrow{\exp} \mathbb{C}$ is continuous as a composition of continuous maps.

title: Kernel = 2π·ℤ ⇒ S¹ ≅ ℝ/2πℤ
content: The kernel `{t : circleMap t = 1}` is exactly `2π·ℤ`, proved via `Complex.exp_eq_one_iff : exp z = 1 ↔ ∃ n, z = n · 2πi`. Specializing to `z = t·i` and cancelling `i` (via `mul_right_cancel₀` since `i ≠ 0`) leaves `t = 2π·n`. The structural consequence is the first isomorphism theorem: `circleHom` factors through `ℝ/2πℤ ≅ S¹` as topological groups. This is the foundation of Fourier analysis on the circle.
mathContext: $\ker(t \mapsto e^{it}) = 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, hence by the first isomorphism theorem $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z} \cong S^1$ as topological groups. The kernel size $2\pi$ encodes the topological non-triviality of $S^1$: $\pi_1(S^1) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, and the universal cover of $S^1$ is $\mathbb{R}$ with deck transformations $2\pi\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Surjectivity via Polar Decomposition
content: Every $z$ on the unit circle has the form `circleMap t` for some real $t$ (concretely, $t = \arg z$). The proof uses `Complex.cos_arg` and `Complex.sin_arg`: when `‖z‖ = 1`, these give `cos(arg z) = z.re` and `sin(arg z) = z.im` (the `/ ‖z‖` factor collapses). Then `Complex.re_add_im z` reconstructs $z = z.re + z.im · i$. Combined with the kernel description, this exhibits `circleHom` as inducing a topological-group isomorphism $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z} \to S^1$.
mathContext: Polar decomposition: every $z \neq 0$ satisfies $z = |z|(\cos(\arg z) + i \sin(\arg z))$. When $|z| = 1$, this is $z = e^{i \arg z}$, so $\arg z$ is the preimage of $z$ under circleMap.

title: De Moivre (ℕ) by Induction on the Homomorphism
content: De Moivre's theorem `(circleMap t)^n = circleMap (n·t)` for natural $n$ is induction: base case `n=0` is `circleMap_zero`; inductive step uses `pow_succ` and `circleMap_add` to fold the new factor. This is the textbook proof of de Moivre, but here it is purely algebraic — no trigonometric identities are invoked.
mathContext: $(e^{it})^n = e^{int}$, equivalently $(\cos t + i \sin t)^n = \cos(nt) + i \sin(nt)$. Historically de Moivre (1722) gave this without complex exponentials; Euler (1748) unified it with $e^{ix} = \cos x + i \sin x$.

title: De Moivre (ℤ) in Four Lines via exp_int_mul
content: The integer version `(circleMap t)^n = circleMap ((n:ℝ)·t)` for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ is even cleaner: `Complex.exp_int_mul` directly states `exp(n·z) = (exp z)^n` for integer $n$. After `push_cast; ring` to align the casts, the proof is four lines. The negative-exponent case is absorbed automatically — no separate handling required, because integer powers of group elements unify positive and negative exponents.
mathContext: $(e^{it})^n = e^{int}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. The negative case $(e^{it})^{-1} = e^{-it}$ is the inverse law of the homomorphism; the integer power law is the sweep over all of $\mathbb{Z}$ given by `Complex.exp_int_mul`.
